title: Coats Disease: Mastering Idiopathic Retinal Telangiectasia
summary: Coats disease is a rare, idiopathic, unilateral condition characterized by progressive retinal telangiectasia and massive subretinal exudation. Essential for the differential of pediatric leukocoria.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Coats disease (idiopathic retinal telangiectasia) is a non-hereditary, idiopathic ocular condition involving idiopathic vascular abnormalities of the retinal capillary bed. Epidemiology: Predominantly affects males (ratio ~3:1). Usually unilateral (90-95%). Typical onset in the first decade of life (mean age 5–10 years). Rare in females and adults.

sections.title: Pathophysiology
content: Breakdown of the inner blood-retina barrier.
Endothelial cell degeneration and pericyte loss.
Telangiectatic vessels leak serum, lipoproteins, and cholesterol.
Formation of massive subretinal/intraretinal 'exudative' deposits (exudative retinal detachment).
Genetic link: Some cases associated with somatic mutations in NDP (Norrie disease protein) gene.

sections.title: Clinical Features & Symptoms
content: Decreased visual acuity (often profound)
Strabismus (esotropia/exotropia)
Leukocoria (white pupillary reflex)
Pain (due to secondary neovascular glaucoma)
Asymptomatic (often missed until late stages)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Dilated Indirect Ophthalmoscopy
Step 2: Wide-field Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) - 'Light bulb' aneurysms
Step 3: B-scan Ultrasonography (to rule out calcified RB)
Step 4: OCT (to document extent of subretinal fluid/exudates)
Step 5: MRI Orbit (if RB suspected to confirm lack of calcification)

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Observation: For very early asymptomatic Stage 1
Laser Photocoagulation: For mild telangiectasia/focal exudation
Cryotherapy: For peripheral lesions or media opacity
Anti-VEGF: Adjuvant for massive exudation/edema
Surgical: Pars Plana Vitrectomy with subretinal drainage

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Calcification on imaging: Highly suggestive of Retinoblastoma (RB), not Coats.
Rapid onset of secondary angle closure glaucoma.
Bilateral presentation: Suspicion shifts toward FEVR or Norrie Disease.
Failure to achieve regression: Re-evaluate for occult malignancy.

content.explanation: C: Capillary telangiectasia, O: Oozing exudates, A: Age (young males), T: Total detachment, S: Shields classification.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always perform an examination under anesthesia (EUA) if RB is not ruled out.
Choroidal findings: Often show reactive non-rhegmatogenous exudative detachment.
Adult-onset Coats is rare and usually milder.
Recurrence: Possible years after treatment; lifelong monitoring required.
